rv.q: But "Topdog" is a relentless play, constantly building in tension and compounding its crises: you have to believe that the pressure on these two brothers is so intense that either of them may explode at any moment, most likely resulting in mutually assured destruction.
It’s not an easy play to digest, but it is a masterful one, and the heavy themes are laced with laugh-out-loud moments throughout.
The show could easily be cut by about 15 minutes with no loss in theme or story.

cn.t: Parks' Pulitzer-winning play about two brothers receives solid praise for its exploration of their fraught bond, though this production doesn't quite reach explosive heights. Strong direction captures the sibling dynamic.
